## System Map: claude-bus broker

`claude-bus` runs a fleet of interactive `claude` TUIs in zellij panes, coordinated by a single broker daemon per session. The broker is the bus's single source of truth. The codebase is layered as a strict library DAG so that the kernel's durability and at-least-once guarantees are protected *by construction* (link boundaries), not by review.

### The areas (8)

| Area | Role | Key files |
|---|---|---|
| **kernel** | persistence + parsing floor: durable append-only log, opaque cursors, topic registry, JSON, event parse | `journal`, `topic_registry`, `json_min`, `event` |
| **readers** | pure read model: substrate → typed views every surface renders | `agent_status`, `task_model`, `trigger_feed`, `pane_state.h`, `tail_reader.h` |
| **policy** | autonomous-behavior seam: actors observe a snapshot, emit declarative actions | `policy`, `recovery_actor`, `recovery`, `dispatch_actor`, `blackboard_actor` |
| **delivery** | the broker's heartbeat: one `Loop::tick()` owns dispatch/ack/retry/epoch + autonomous behaviors | `delivery.{h,cpp}` (~1740 lines) |
| **broker** | daemon shell: lifecycle, singleton flock, per-boot wipe, epoch bump, RPC handler registry | `broker`, `signals.h`, `state_paths.h`, `retention.h` |
| **rpc** | wire layer (line-JSON over unix socket) + two-thread reactor; TTY dispatch state machine | `rpc`, `dispatch` |
| **pane** | the only bridge to zellij TUIs: ANSI-scrape read, draft-safe write, TTL caches | `pane`, `pane_state.h`, `tty_policy.h` |
| **cli** | unified `bus` binary: flat registry dispatcher, ~27 subcommands | `bus_main`, `bus`, `sub/sub_*` |

### Library DAG (the structural fence)

```
bus_core  ─────────────────────────────┐  (journal, topic_registry, json_min, event,
   │                                    │   state_paths, retention, signals)
   ├──> bus_readers ──> bus_policy      │   bus_readers links bus_core + bus_envelope ONLY,
   │      (agent_status,   (policy,     │   NEVER bus_pane → a reader cannot name paneState();
   │       task_model,      recovery,   │   bus_policy adds no pane lib, no socket → an actor
   │       trigger_feed)    actors)     │   that reaches for a cursor verb or pane fails to BUILD.
   │                                    │
   ├──> bus_pane (pane.cpp; the zellij bridge) ──> bus_envelope
   │                                    │
   └──> the `bus` binary (delivery.cpp, broker.cpp, rpc.cpp, dispatch.cpp, bus_main.cpp, sub/*)
              links everything above.
```

The split is load-bearing: `pane_state.h` (the value struct) is split out of `pane.h` (the acquisition API) so the Readers seam consumes a *snapshot* without being able to name the fork. `nm`-verified link guards (`eba57df0` technique) make these boundaries mechanical.

### Data flow (one tick)

```
hooks ──write──> events.jsonl ─┐
$STATE/{done,triggers,status}  │
broker topic logs (Journal)    ├─ READERS (pure, no authority) ─> AgentSnapshot / PolicyContext
injected PaneState snapshot ───┘            │
                                            v
                              POLICY ENGINE (observe → guard → emit)
                              actors return DECLARATIVE actions (Enqueue|Recover|Nudge,
                              + consume_from); NO cursor verb exists.
                                            │
                                            v
                              DELIVERY Loop::tick()  (the only state mutator)
                              scanEvents → onAck → dispatch → escalate → runPolicy
                                            │
                              ┌─────────────┴──────────────┐
                       off-TTY drain hook            TTY dispatchTui (comms only)
                       (additionalContext + doorbell)  (flock + sendToPaneSafe)
                                            │
                                            v
                                   PANE  (zellij action) ──> live claude TUI
```

CLI tools talk to the broker via JSON-RPC on `$STATE/broker.sock`; the RPC reactor is split into an **intake** thread (accept/parse/hand off the conn fd) and a single **processing** thread (owns ALL broker state, runs handlers + the delivery tick off a timerfd). One processing thread ⇒ zero locking ⇒ free atomicity, the property every other pillar leans on.

### The kernel triad (the contended invariant the whole system protects)

1. **Append-only Log** — `bus::Journal`, one file per topic, byte offsets stable forever; CRC+trailer framing makes a torn tail self-truncating; payloads are OPAQUE bytes.
2. **Cursor advances ONLY on ack** — never on dispatch. An un-acked record sits at the head and re-delivers when the recipient is ready, so retry is *free*. `Cursor` is opaque (friend-minted, forward-only `ack`, `.lastid` dedup floor); `Loop::onAck` is the SOLE advance path.
3. **Boot-epoch stamp** — every record carries the current epoch (in the Envelope payload); a stale-epoch record is escalated + cursor-advanced, never delivered. This lets a per-boot wipe of *volatile* state coexist with a *durable* on-disk log without re-delivering yesterday's mail.

The policy seam protects this triad mechanically: the action vocabulary has no `AdvanceCursor`, and `bus_policy` cannot link the socket or pane — so the worst a buggy actor can do is emit an auditable record.

## Per-area briefs (what / why-shaped / why-VALUABLE / tensions)

Each brief is for a guided 1:1 review: what it is, why it took this shape, why it earns its place, and the live tensions to surface (not resolve). Doc-vs-code divergences are flagged because several specs lag the code.

---

### 1. kernel — `src/journal.{h,cpp}`, `topic_registry.{h,cpp}`, `json_min.{h,cpp}`, `event.{h,cpp}`

**What.** The broker's persistence + parsing floor, no broker logic. `Journal` is a durable append-only log of OPAQUE byte records (v6 wire: crc32c | front len | append_ms | seq | payload | trailer len), CRC-verified-before-parse, torn-tail self-truncating, torn-write rollback, with the cursor store under `$STATE/cursors/`. Its `Cursor` is opaque (offset + FNV tag, forward-only `ack`, `.lastid` dedup). `topic_registry` is the declarative `kind` table delivery routes on. `json_min` is the hand-rolled, float-free, depth-256-capped JSON. `event` parses one `events.jsonl` line, reading the *nested* `payload` shape.

**Why this shape.** One pressure: a single-writer, crash-and-reboot-survivable system-of-record the rest of the broker builds on without re-deriving durability. Single-writer makes reads lock-free and the pre-write size capture race-free; CRC+trailer makes a torn tail unambiguous; opaque payloads let one log serve any record shape (the epoch was pushed OUT into the Envelope); opaque Cursor structurally enforces at-least-once; hand-rolled JSON because the broker owns both ends and wanted a hard depth cap (a deep-`[` payload once blew the stack).

**Why VALUABLE.** This is the ONLY layer converting "bytes on disk" into "a record that survived a crash." Drop the CRC/torn-tail logic → a power-loss tail parses as garbage / OOB read. Expose raw offsets → at-least-once collapses, any caller can fabricate or rewind a cursor. Drop `trimHead`'s cursor rebase → the first retention trim shifts every live cursor. Drop the `kind` → delivery loses its ack-on-dispatch-vs-fetch decision. Drop the depth cap → a hostile `[[[…` SIGSEGVs the broker. Flatten `event`'s parse → cross-agent status reads the wrong agent (the C3 misparse).

**Tensions to surface.** (a) STALE: `broker-spec.md §"Where the epoch lives"` claims a 16-byte `correlation` field in `topic_log.h` — that class is now `journal`, the v6 wire has NO correlation field, the epoch lives in the Envelope payload. A redesign MUST choose: make a first-class epoch field real, or formally bless "epoch-in-envelope, journal-opaque." (b) Opaque payload means the kernel can enforce NOTHING about the envelope (epoch fence, content dedup) — all that lives a layer up. (c) Two Journal constructors create two capability tiers (raw-I/O vs full) the type system does NOT distinguish; ack/trim CRASH on the wrong tier. (d) Single-writer is load-bearing but UNCHECKED — a second writer silently breaks id uniqueness. (e) `tail()`'s torn-tail fallback is O(whole log).

---

### 2. readers — `src/agent_status`, `task_model`, `trigger_feed`, `pane_state.h`, `tail_reader.h` (lib `bus_readers`)

**What.** The fleet's pure read model: turns durable substrate (`events.jsonl`, `$STATE/{done,triggers,status}`, the `tasks` topic log, an injected `PaneState`) into typed views. `readAgents`+`foldTurnState`+`computeAxes` project four orthogonal axes (Process/Turn/Mail/Tui); `computeState` collapses them to the legacy `State`; `wakeReadyForMail` is the doorbell predicate. `readTasks` joins three stores by id; `buildTaskGraph` derives ready/blocked/chain/cycle from deps. `trigger_feed` computes URGENCY×SAFETY for the P3 watchdog. `tail_reader.h` is the extracted append-log tail primitive.

**Why this shape.** Three pressures: (1) ONE derivation, MANY surfaces — monitor, agent-bar, `bus tasks`, the state RPC, and the doorbell must never disagree, so derivation is pure free functions every surface calls. (2) NO AUTHORITY — readers own no mutable state; every output reconstructs from substrate + injected snapshot, so the seam is unit-testable with a fake Log and no socket. `pane_state.h` makes this STRUCTURAL (a stray `paneState()` is a compile error). (3) The single `State` enum LIES under uncertainty (wedged-vs-quiet is invisible under `state = f(last_event)`), so the model went orthogonal-axes, and the continuity clamp stops a reboot's wall-clock leap from flipping the fleet false-STUCK.

**Why VALUABLE.** Collapse back to `state = f(last_event)` → lose wedged-vs-quiet AND the display stops agreeing with `maybeEscalateStuck`, so cockpit and recovery disagree about who is stuck. Drop the continuity clamp → every lid-close paints false-STUCK on resume. Drop `wakeReadyForMail` → the doorbell pushes mid-stream or never wakes idle agents. Centralization is the whole point — without it the two-surface disagreement returns. `task_model`'s reconcile-by-id shows open/in_flight/done without a fourth store and degrades gracefully; `buildTaskGraph`'s cycle guard stops a dep loop hanging the viewer.

**Tensions to surface.** (a) NAMESPACE: the seam doc proposes `bus::readers`; code stayed flat `bus::` and enforces the seam purely at the LINK/INCLUDE layer — decide if the boundary is namespace or link (it's link, today). (b) `verify` is *called* a reader by the doc but lives in `sub_verify.cpp`, NOT in `bus_readers` — the doc counts four readers, the lib has three. (c) `tail_reader` is the reference impl but wired to NOTHING — the broker's three inline copies aren't rewired, and `readAgents` itself full-re-reads `events.jsonl` every call (the exact pattern it exists to replace). (d) `computeState` is an explicit compat SHIM; the axes-everywhere migration is incomplete. (e) `in_flight` is INFERRED (owner-live), not proven; deps are empty until dispatch mints identity, so the graph is built ahead of its data. (f) Orchestrating is mail-RECEPTIVE in `agent_status` but an UNSAFE boundary in `trigger_feed` — both readings are intentional, don't unify.

---

### 3. policy — `src/policy`, `recovery_actor`, `recovery`, `dispatch_actor`, `blackboard_actor` (lib `bus_policy`)

**What.** The broker's autonomous-behavior seam: a tiny engine the delivery loop runs each tick. Actors observe a read-only `PolicyContext`, apply their own guards, and return DECLARATIVE `PolicyAction`s (`Enqueue|Recover|Nudge`, plus `consume_from`). `PolicyEngine` is ~28 lines of fan-out, owns no broker resource. `recovery_actor` is the reference: the P2 triage (R1 idle→clear, R2 relaunch-idle→nudge, R3 hung-turn, R4 wedged) with breaker/backoff; `recovery.{h,cpp}` is its PURE broker-free core (monotonic-clock breaker, boot_id reset). `dispatch_actor` is the work-queue claim pattern (1→1); `blackboard_actor` is stateless fan-out (1→N).

**Why this shape.** One constraint everywhere in `docs/policy-actors.md`: autonomous behavior must NOT perturb the kernel triad. So: (1) god-object avoidance — adding a behavior is a `registerActor` call, not a new Loop method. (2) Kernel-safety BY CONSTRUCTION — the vocabulary omits any cursor verb, and the LINK boundary (`bus_policy` links readers+core only) means an actor reaching for a cursor/pane fails to BUILD. (3) Purity — clocks and a lazy pane resolver arrive via `ctx`, so no real time/pane crosses the seam. (4) No engine arbitration — two actors on one target resolve at execution via existing in-flight/breaker gating (arbitration would be the god-object creeping back). (5) The pure recovery core is carved out so the safety-critical breaker is unit-testable with synthetic clocks; monotonic+boot_id stops a lid-close mass-firing recovery.

**Why VALUABLE.** Fold actors back into the Loop and three things regress: the triad loses its STRUCTURAL fence (a recovery bug could then double-advance a cursor); coordination patterns lose their cheap central home (a work-queue becomes ~40 lines reusing broker primitives instead of per-agent racing Stop hooks); recovery loses unit-testability and suspend-safety. This is sulin's north-star single coordination substrate ("an agent IS a composition of policies").

**Tensions to surface.** (a) DOC↔CODE: `consume_from` exists in the struct but NOT in the doc's vocabulary section (intentional M2 extension). (b) `Recover`/`Nudge` are vocabulary-only — `executePolicyAction` handles them as a bare `break;`; recovery NEVER relaunches today (R4 only logs would-recover). (c) R2's would-recover duplicates the doorbell's exact predicate — two paths encode one readiness rule (the doc proposes folding the doorbell in as a NudgeActor). (d) Arbitration is a DELIBERATE punt, design-complete only because every current action is idempotent; the revisit-trigger (a non-idempotent conflicting pair) is documented. (e) The pure-core split is held by DISCIPLINE — clock/socket/fs creep into `recovery.cpp` breaks testability with no compile error. (f) R5/R6 (thinking-block-400, ctx-100%) are stubs — the destructive correctness rungs are NOT implemented. (g) Coordination retirement ("patterns = pure actors") is aspirational; re-queue-on-death genuinely is NOT a pure actor (needs ack awareness).

### 4. delivery — `src/delivery.{h,cpp}` (~1740 lines)

**What.** The broker's autonomous heartbeat: `Loop::tick()` runs each reactor wake (RPC arrival / 250ms floor / deadline timerfd). One tick in order: updateContinuity → scanEvents (ack in-flight) → scanRetries → maybeAutoClear → runPolicy → maybeScanTokens (CTX%) → maybeWakeIdleOffTty (doorbell) → maybeTrimLogs → dispatch per topic → maybeEscalateStuck. It OWNS: dispatch (gate ladder + one record/tick/topic via `sendToPaneSafe`), ack+cursors (the cursor advances ONLY via `onAck`→`Journal::ack`, fed by three arms: positional UPS, explicit `bus-ack`, blocking-op Stop), the in-flight lifecycle, epoch fencing, and the autonomous behaviors (auto-clear, doorbell, strand watchdog, stuck escalation, token scan, retention, GC, the PolicyEngine).

**Why this shape.** Forced by one constraint: recipients are interactive TUIs the human also drives, with NO reliable delivery receipt. So: cursor-advances-only-on-ack (the head record stays put until a downstream event is observed; retry is free re-evaluation). IN-FLIGHT ⟹ ALREADY-DELIVERED for agent-inbox (a record is in-flight only AFTER the write succeeds, so a missed ack-deadline must NOT re-type — that garbles the buffer; the retry timer escalates, doesn't re-deliver). Off-TTY-by-default + doorbell (an idle off-TTY agent takes no turns, so its drain hook never fires — the `[bus-wake]` sentinel manufactures a turn boundary). One tick, many cadence-gated scans (the single thread is the only log writer; a pane fork is 5s-capped, so per-agent reads every tick would starve RPC — the documented saturation wedge). Policy seam so new behaviors register against a fixed interface instead of re-fusing the 74KB god-object.

**Why VALUABLE.** This IS the reliability story. Drop ack-gated cursors → at-most-once (a scrolled/locked pane silently loses mail). Drop in-flight⟹delivered → the dup-delivery bug returns (same mail typed 3×). Drop epoch fencing → either keep all volatile state forever or re-deliver yesterday's mail + risk an infinite self-escalation loop. Drop the doorbell → idle off-TTY agents never receive queued mail. Drop the cadence gates → the broker starves its own RPC under fan-out. Drop in-tick retention → logs grow unbounded on the durable root.

**Tensions to surface.** (a) STALE header (delivery.h 15-26) claims retry + tui-dispatch are "Deferred" — both are implemented here now. (b) DOC↔CODE: spec says retry-exhaustion mails `inbox-human`; code mails `inbox-OPS`. (c) POSITIONAL TTY ACK FRAGILITY (acknowledged): a UPS acks the OLDEST in-flight record, so a human typing at the pane can burn an ack against the wrong record; off-TTY fixed this via `bus-ack` by msg_id — open follow-up. (d) Retry is per-kind and subtle: agent-inbox = ack-DEADLINE-escalate-only; tui-slashes genuinely re-dispatch and are NOT yet exactly-once. (e) The pane-read fork on the delivery thread is the latent wedge ("stop pane-reading" is the structural fix). (f) maybeAutoClear stands aside when AUTO_RECOVERY is on (R1 owns it) — mode-coupling the unfinished AutoClearActor fold would dissolve. (g) Continuity handling is deliberately duplicated from recovery's own grace.

---

### 5. broker — `src/broker.{h,cpp}`, `signals.h`, `state_paths.h`, `retention.h`

**What.** The daemon SHELL (not the engine). `runBroker()` is process lifecycle + the RPC handler registry: (1) acquire a singleton flock on `broker.pid` with orphan-takeover (reap a PPID-1 corpse, DEFER to a live broker); (2) `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`; (3) surgically wipe per-boot VOLATILE state (`in-flight/`, `presence/`, `tui-locks/`, `broker.sock`) while PRESERVING `topics/`, `cursors/`, `agents/`, `payloads/`, `broker.epoch`, `events.jsonl`; (4) wire-format migration (wipe only on stale version); (5) bump+persist the epoch; (6) load the registry; (7) register ~17 RPC handlers (the handlers carry real coordination logic — pubsub cascade, blackboard fast-forward, the C1 single-recipient cursor normalization, the fetch/drain in-flight skip, the D3 off-TTY drain ack logic, broker-GC); (8) `server.run(250ms, dl.tick, dl.nextDeadlineMs)`. `signals.h` uses `sa_flags=0` (NOT SA_RESTART) so blocking syscalls EINTR and the stop flag is seen. `state_paths.h` is the single durable XDG root. `retention.h` is pure trim math with `clamp_to_cursor`.

**Why this shape.** (1) At-least-once + dedup + restart-safety from ONE mechanism (offset log + ack-only cursor + epoch); the boot wipe+epoch bump is the machinery that makes "durable log that never re-delivers yesterday's mail" true. (2) Single processing thread → zero locking → free atomicity (the property every pillar leans on). (3) The daemon must die with its session and exactly one must run — flock+orphan-reap+PDEATHSIG exists because a `nohup`-backgrounded broker survives a zellij restart, keeps the flock, answers the socket, but its `zellij action` calls hit a DEAD session and it DEFER-blocks every new session forever. (4) `$STATE` became durable (off `/tmp` tmpfs) which FORCED retention to exist. (5) `sa_flags=0` is forced by a concrete hang (SA_RESTART auto-resumes the syscall so the stop flag is never re-checked).

**Why VALUABLE.** Drop the epoch fence / surgical wipe → re-deliver yesterday's whole queue OR throw away audit logs every boot. Drop the flock+reap → two brokers in one bus, or a corpse that DEFER-blocks every future session silently. Drop C1 normalization → an arbitrary `--consumer` splits the cursor namespace (the `inbox-<name>` vs `<name>` drift). Drop the fetch/drain in-flight skip → the `/loop fetch` fallback races the push path and double-delivers. Drop `clamp_to_cursor` → expiry drops undelivered mail. Drop non-SA_RESTART → SIGTERM hangs to SIGKILL. Drop XDG durability → a reboot wipes logs/cursors/epoch.

**Tensions to surface.** (a) STALE header: `broker.h` claims "Phase 4b.1 skeleton… only a ping op" — there are ~17 handlers, delivery, GC. (b) DOC/CODE wire version: spec says "v4" in ~4 places; code is version-agnostic via `kJournalFormatVersion` — confirm the real number before citing one. (c) DOC/CODE threading: `broker.cpp` inline comments still describe the OLD single-thread model; the two-thread split lives in `rpc.cpp` (handler code is unchanged BY DESIGN, but a reader trusting the comments gets the threading wrong). (d) DEAD CONFIG: `max_record_bytes` is enforced by nothing; `retention_ms`=0 everywhere so age-expiry is DORMANT (only the byte cap is live). (e) Blackboard enqueue opens a SECOND Journal handle to one log. (f) RPC handlers do REAL policy (pubsub cascade, audit appends) inline in `runBroker` — the "agent as policies" north-star would pull these out.

---

### 6. rpc — `src/rpc.{h,cpp}`, `dispatch.{h,cpp}`

**What.** Two concerns. (1) `rpc` is the wire layer: line-delimited JSON-RPC over a 0600 unix socket; one connection = one request + reply + close. `rpc::call()` is the one-shot client every CLI tool uses. `rpc::Server::run()` is split into an INTAKE thread (only accept/read/parse one request, hand the live conn_fd to a queue) and a single PROCESSING thread (dequeue, run the handler against state it SOLELY owns, write reply, close fd, drive the tick off its own timerfd + 250ms floor). Backpressure: a full bounded queue is shed with a constant "broker busy, retry" string (no state touched). Hardening: SOCK_NONBLOCK listen fd, 5s SO_RCVTIMEO/SNDTIMEO, inode-guarded socket unlink in `~Server`, a static `gStopFlag` polled by both loops. (2) `dispatch` is the TTY delivery state machine (lifted from `bin/dispatch-tui`): `dispatchTui` resolves the pane, takes the per-pane flock, then up to 3 attempts (0.25/1/4s backoff) — write if ready (INSERT + empty buffer), else normalize (Esc Esc + i) and retry; polls `stopRequested()` between every step.

**Why this shape.** The dominant pressure is the "free atomicity" the broker leans on. The two failure modes the split solves: (1a) the fan-out wedge — the tick forks zellij per agent (5s-capped dump-screen), serializing into tens of seconds while the single thread is NOT at accept(), so the recv-queue backs up and the broker is "alive by the clock yet effectively down" (the live 2026-05-31 outage); (1b) RPC-driven-tick fragility — with one pselect, the idle timeout was EINTR-starved, so time-based work only advanced when a viewer polled ~1Hz. The split keeps processing the SOLE owner of all state BY CONSTRUCTION (the fd is handed off, not read on intake, because EVERY handler touches processing-owned state), while a slow tick can't starve accept(). The timerfd makes the tick self-drive. `dispatch`'s shape is forced by the TTY being a shared, human-occupied surface (flock serializes against `bus msg send`; INSERT+empty + Esc-Esc-i normalize; backoff absorbs transient non-readiness; in-process so no per-delivery fork cost).

**Why VALUABLE.** Collapse run() to one thread → the fan-out wedge returns immediately (a real outage; `tests/decouple-itest.sh` keeps it dead). Drop the timerfd/floor → time-based delivery stalls on a quiet fleet (the "RPC-responsive but stops pushing" wedge class). Drop bounded backpressure → a fast producer blows memory or parks every client. Drop the SOCK_NONBLOCK + EINTR-rechecks → a stalled client or a SIGTERM mid-accept wedges shutdown (the TC48 orphan-pileup root). Drop the inode-guard → a shutting-down broker unlinks a successor's socket. On dispatch: drop the flock → interleaved garbage in the human's pane; drop readiness/normalize → deliveries land in NORMAL mode or onto a half-typed draft and are lost.

**Tensions to surface.** (a) DOC/CODE: the doc specs epoll{eventfd,timerfd}; code uses pselect for BOTH threads (equivalent at this fd count, but epoll was never built). (b) Queue depth: doc says 1024, code defaults to 256. (c) Shutdown handshake: doc specs a `stop` RPC + `::shutdown(listen_fd)` to kick intake; code does NOT — both loops poll `gStopFlag`, intake notices within one 250ms poll (confirm against the SIGTERM-shutdown-wedge history). (d) FD-OWNERSHIP: once enqueued, processing owns `close()` on EVERY path; intake closes only fds it never enqueued — break it for a double-close or fd-leak→EMFILE. (e) TIMERFD CLOCK SEAM: rearm mixes a system_clock deadline into a CLOCK_MONOTONIC timer, so a wall-jump (lid-close) skews the next fire; past-due clamps to 1ms (never 0), and the escalate-once contract stops a busy-loop. (f) `dispatchTui` is SYNCHRONOUS (~5.25s worst case) — the last blocking op the tick can reach; `isReady` keys on EXACT strings (`mode=='INSERT'`, `buffer=='(empty)'`), so a pane-render change silently breaks it. (g) Live typo `[bus-wak[bus-wake]e]` in `dispatch.cpp:42`.

### 7. pane — `src/pane.{h,cpp}`, `pane_state.h`, `tty_policy.h`

**What.** The single ANSI-aware bridge between the broker and the live zellij TUIs. READ: `paneState(name)` forks `zellij action dump-screen --ansi`, strips/parses ANSI into a `PaneState` (mode, the human's `buffer`, claude's ghost `suggestion`, `bypass_perms`); `paneId` resolves a name to `terminal_N` by hand-parsing list-panes. WRITE: `sendToPane` (raw + Enter, newlines→spaces), `sendKey`, and `sendToPaneSafe` (the draft-preserving inbox write: snapshot draft, refuse on unknown/LOCKED/bypass-off, force a clean INSERT line, write, re-type the draft). COST: two TTL caches (`paneStateCached` 300ms, `listPanesJsonCached` 3000ms), single-threaded, owned by the broker loop. `tty_policy.h` is the compiled-in routing switch (only `comms` + `$CLAUDE_BUS_TTY_AGENTS` go via TTY-push; the fleet default is off-TTY). `pane_state.h` holds just the value struct.

**Why this shape.** The fundamental constraint: zellij exposes NO API — the only channel to a claude TUI is shelling out and scraping the rendered screen. Every shape falls out of that colliding with two others. (a) The broker is single-threaded and every `zellij` call is on its delivery thread, so a hung dump-screen halts the loop → forces `runCapture`'s deadline+SIGKILL, the 5s cap, the fork-before-malloc child path, and BOTH caches (the 2026-05-31 fan-out wedge was N back-to-back list-panes forks per scan). (b) Reading a rendered terminal is lossy and adversarial (footer padding, cursor inverting the first ghost char, divider on the prompt row, U+00A0 NBSP padding, scrolled/locked panes unreadable) → `unknown` as a first-class "refuse, don't guess" mode and a whole-screen (not bottom-N) scan. (c) Writing into a pane the human may be typing in forces the read-modify-restore dance and the `\n`-to-space flatten. `tty_policy` is compiled-in because a `$STATE` sentinel kept getting wiped on relaunch.

**Why VALUABLE.** This file is the accreted scar tissue of every way terminal-scraping has bitten the fleet. Drop the caches → the single-threaded broker re-forks N queries per scan and wedges (the 2026-05-31 outage). Drop the deadline/SIGKILL → one hung `zellij action` freezes the loop indefinitely. Replace the whole-screen scan with bottom-N → footer-variant panes defer delivery forever (the bast-wedge) and blank footers misread as BootStuck. Drop sendToPaneSafe's refusals → the broker writes mail into scrolled history or a human approval prompt. Drop the `\n`-flatten/draft restore → human keystrokes merge into injected messages (the comms TTY-clobber). Drop fork-before-malloc → a child deadlocks on the malloc arena lock.

**Tensions to surface.** (a) DOC/CODE: `docs/pane-read-audit.md` cites `readPaneState` at `agent_status.h:206` — that symbol no longer exists (folded into `paneState()` by the Readers-seam extraction); the audit's FINDINGS hold, the line/symbol refs are stale. (b) THE BIG OPEN LEVER: the broker pays a full per-agent dump-screen on every ~1Hz state RPC to surface fields the monitor mostly DOESN'T render (`buffer`/`mode`/`bypass` fetched then `(void)`'d away) — actual need reduces to pane_exists + a mode supplement; this is the heart of sulin's first-class "stop pane-reading" goal (pane I/O should become FALLBACK). (c) HEURISTIC FRAGILITY: detectMode/detectBypass/parseInput depend on exact claude-TUI rendering (the greyscale ramp, U+276F prompt, U+2500 divider) — a TUI restyle silently breaks them, no upstream guarantee. (d) Single-threaded cache coupling — lock-free ONLY because the broker owns the thread; a multi-threaded broker invalidates this everywhere. (e) sendToPaneSafe truncates multi-line drafts to one row (the comms multiline strand). (f) Write timing is blind sleeps (50/100ms), no readback-confirm. (g) FORK COST IS STRUCTURAL — a persistent zellij IPC channel would dissolve most of this file.

---

### 8. cli — `src/bus_main.cpp`, `bus.cpp`, `sub/sub_*.cpp`

**What.** The unified `bus` surface: one binary, one dispatcher, ~27 top-level subcommands (plus sub-verbs under `msg`/`topic`/`tasks`/`broker`). `bus_main.cpp` matches argv[1] against a flat registry (`kSubcommands`) and hands the rest as `std::span` to a handler with one shared signature `int(span)`. `printUsage` walks the SAME registry, so help can't drift from dispatch. Handler shapes: (1) thin RPC clients (topic, produce/consume, state, inflight); (2) `$STATE` file stores that never touch the broker (`done`, `task set`, `verify`, `tasks`, `triggers`); (3) zellij/TTY actuators (`pane-id`, `msg send`, `spawn`/`despawn`/`recover`); (4) long-running viewers (`monitor`, `tasks watch`, `inbox`, `events`, `log`, `agent-bar`). Exit convention: usage→2, runtime→1, ok→0 (with `recover` adding 10/20/30 as the breaker's signal channel).

**Why this shape.** "Everything through one binary" (CLAUDE.md) replacing a pile of shell scripts. A flat function-pointer registry is the minimum mechanism giving one dispatch point, one help source, one handler contract. The `span`-in/`int`-out signature is C-shaped so a handler `return`s a process exit code and forwards argv cheaply to sub-dispatchers via `subspan(1)`. The broker-vs-direct split: the broker owns all topic state (so produce/consume are RPC wrappers), but the durable-completion path (`done`/`verify`) deliberately BYPASSES the broker — `done` writes a plain append-only file so the claim survives a broker restart, a `/clear`, and orchestrator relay failures (exactly what `verify` catches). Parity-during-migration freezes `pane-id`/`msg send` output byte-for-byte (shell hooks still parse it). Anti-lie discipline: `tasks` ERRORS on an unknown verb rather than falling through to an empty table (a mistyped verb once read as authoritative "no tasks" and fooled the hub into minting dupes). Exit-code-as-protocol: `recover`'s 0/10/20/30 ARE the interface the recovery engine reads.

**Why VALUABLE.** Drop the registry+uniform-signature spine → help drifts from behavior (an agent-facing tool whose `help` lies). Collapse the per-file `sub_*.cpp` split → reintroduce merge contention (separate files are how 5 concurrent agents in separate jj workspaces edit the CLI; the registry array is the only shared touch-point). Drop the broker-bypass file stores → the "claimed-but-absent" false-completion alarm dies with the broker (the most-hit failure mode, which MUST NOT depend on the broker being healthy). Flatten `recover`'s exit codes → the breaker can't tell "booted but stuck" (10) from "never came up" (20) from "human on the pane, don't touch" (30) — it kills agents under a human or loops on a boot-stuck pane.

**Tensions to surface.** (a) DOC STALE — the biggest finding: `docs/bus-commands.md` documents 23 surfaces; the registry has 27 + many sub-verbs. Undocumented: agents, introduce, roles, verify, triggers, tasks, task, done, log, recover, despawn, restore-peers, state-root, msg drain/drop (~40% under-count). Specific contradictions: doc says `broker run` is the only broker verb (code has run|info|gc); doc says spawn uses `agent-launch` for session-UUID discovery (UUIDs are GONE); doc says `msg mail --title` writes the TASK column (it's INERT, `task set` owns it now). (b) NAMING DRIFT: `bus task` (monitor column writer) vs `bus tasks` (task-model reader) are one keystroke apart, and subTask/subDone physically live in `sub_produce.cpp`. (c) Two parallel families BY DESIGN (broker-RPC vs broker-free file stores) — any "unify the data path" redesign must preserve done/verify's broker-independence. (d) Arg parsing is hand-rolled + duplicated ~15× with subtle divergences — a naive unification risks changing frozen-format behavior. (e) Unknown-verb policy is INCONSISTENT (`tasks` errors loudly by design; `msg` returns 1; `topic`/`broker` return 2). (f) Three independent "where am I" re-derivations (selfDir, rolesDir with a hardcoded `/home/sulin/claude-bus` fallback, stateRoot). (g) Viewers re-implement the same alt-screen loop per file (and die silently leaving a frozen frame — robustness matters more than DRY here).


---

## Guided reading path

Read bottom-up: each layer's guarantees become the assumptions the next layer builds on. Read each area's design doc BEFORE its code so the code reads as "implements X" not "discover X."

### Hop 1 — kernel (the floor)
Start at `src/journal.h` (the wire-format header comment + the `Cursor` doc ARE the mental model), then `journal.cpp` in order append → ParseFromBuffer → ack/trimHead, then `topic_registry.cpp::getOrAutoCreate`, with `json_min` + `event` as the leaf dependencies.
*Reason:* the kernel triad (append-only Log, cursor-advances-on-ack, boot-epoch) is the contended invariant EVERYTHING above protects — you can't reason about delivery or policy until "a record survived a crash" and "a cursor only moves forward on ack" are concrete.

### Hop 2 — readers (the pure projection)
`pane_state.h` first (the seam boundary), then `agent_status.h` (the vocabulary: events, the fold accumulator, the four axes), then `agent_status.cpp` (readAgents → foldTurnState → computeAxes → wakeReadyForMail), then `trigger_feed` and `task_model`.
*Reason:* readers turn the kernel's substrate into the typed views every surface AND the policy snapshot consume — and they introduce no new authority, so they're the cleanest layer to learn the fleet's state model before anything mutates it.

### Hop 3 — policy (the autonomous seam)
`docs/policy-actors.md` first (§1.4 no-cursor-verb, §2.1 no-arbitration, §4 the leaf guard), then `policy.h`, then `recovery.h`→`recovery.cpp` (the pure breaker), then `recovery_actor.cpp::evaluate`.
*Reason:* policy consumes the reader snapshot and emits DECLARATIVE actions; understanding that an actor literally cannot name a cursor or a socket (by link boundary) is the key to seeing how the triad stays safe under autonomous behavior — read it before the loop that runs it.

### Hop 4 — delivery (the heartbeat that mutates)
`delivery.h` in full (the invariants are stated as doc-comments), then `delivery.cpp`: tick() (the index) → onAck → scanEvents → scanRetries → dispatchAgentInbox → escalate, then the autonomous behaviors, then runPolicy.
*Reason:* this is where reader-snapshots and policy-actions become real cursor advances, pane writes, and escalations — the single thread that enforces ack-gated cursors, in-flight⟹delivered, and epoch fencing. It only makes sense once you hold the kernel triad and know what a reader/actor hands it.

### Hop 5 — broker / rpc (the shell + reactor that drives the tick)
`docs/broker-spec.md` (the 3-primitive kernel) and `docs/broker-intake-decouple.md` §1–§3 first, then `state_paths.h` + `signals.h`, then `broker.cpp::runBroker` top-to-bottom (lifecycle 220-394, then the handler registry), then `rpc.cpp::Server::run` (the intake/processing split + timerfd) and `dispatch.cpp::dispatchTui`.
*Reason:* the broker is the lifecycle + handler shell that constructs the Loop and the epoch fence; rpc is the two-thread reactor whose single processing thread is WHY delivery needs no locks. Read them after delivery so "free atomicity" and "self-driving tick" attach to code you already understand.

### Hop 6 — pane (the bridge delivery reaches through)
`pane_state.h` (re-anchor the value type), `pane.h` (the contract + cache/draft rationale), then `pane.cpp`: the subprocess plumbing (runCapture) → the ANSI parser (detectMode/parseInput) → the composed public functions (paneState, sendToPaneSafe), then `tty_policy.h`.
*Reason:* pane is the lossy, hang-prone zellij-scraping channel every dispatch and every reader-pane-fork ultimately depends on — read it after delivery/broker so its caching, deadlines, and refuse-don't-guess heuristics read as answers to wedges you've already seen named upstream.

### Hop 7 — cli (the surface a human/agent drives)
`bus_main.cpp` (dispatch) → `bus.h`/`sub.h` (the contract) → `bus.cpp` (the registry = the index of everything), then `docs/bus-commands.md` held against the registry to see the ~40% it omits, then the handler files (`sub_msg`, `sub_produce`, `sub_lifecycle`, `sub_verify`).
*Reason:* the CLI is the thin client layer over everything below — RPC wrappers, broker-free durable-claim file stores, and TTY actuators — so it reads fastest LAST, when you can already place each handler against the broker, kernel store, or pane path it actually drives.
